evidence: src/infrastructure/http/BadRequestError.ts: `class BadRequestError extends Error` is documented as 'Raised when an HTTP request is malformed before it reaches a use case', which is an HTTP-only concern.

src/infrastructure/http/RequestReader.ts: `optionalString` and `requiredString` both read fields through the private `fieldOf`. `requiredString` builds on `optionalString`, and errors are reported only through `throw new BadRequestError(...)`.

src/infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts: `STATUS_BY_KIND: Record<DomainErrorKind, number>` plus the `instanceof BadRequestError` and `isMalformedJson` branches put all error-to-status mapping in one place.
src/infrastructure/http/createApp.ts: `createApp(deps)` registers express.json, the route modules, a 404 fallback and `app.use(errorHandler)` last. It has no error-mapping logic of its own.

Small overlap: the 404 fallback in createApp.ts (`res.status(404).json({ error: 'Route not found' })`) uses the same `{ error }` response shape as errorHandler.ts. It is a shared output format, not a duplicated rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The four files all deal with one thing: the Express HTTP adapter. createApp.ts builds the app and registers the middleware. RequestReader.ts checks request fields. BadRequestError.ts defines the error for malformed requests. middleware/errorHandler.ts turns errors into HTTP responses. The module's own abstractions are used consistently. RequestReader reports bad input only by throwing BadRequestError. errorHandler is the single place that maps errors to status codes: it uses STATUS_BY_KIND for domain errors and handles BadRequestError and malformed JSON there too. createApp installs errorHandler last instead of handling errors itself. Field checking is defined once: requiredString builds on optionalString, and both share the private fieldOf helper. The only overlap is small. createApp's inline 404 handler writes the same { error } response shape that errorHandler uses. That is a shared output format, not a duplicated business rule or invariant, so it does not count as a violation. Import direction was not judged because it is out of scope.
